notes: How house lordship changes a planet's nature for each ascendant (verses 19-44), plus the general principles of verses 2-17. Each verse also names 'maraka' planets; those statements are omitted under the sensitive-topics policy.

skipped.reason: Rahu/Ketu act for their dispositor and companions; needs a dispositor predicate the matcher does not have yet.

rules.text: Reading principle: lords of the trines (1st, 5th, 9th) always give good results; natural benefics lose some of their benefit, and natural malefics some of their harm, when they rule an angle (4th, 7th, 10th); lords of the 3rd, 6th and 11th give difficult results; lords of the 2nd, 8th and 12th act according to the planets they are associated with and the other house they rule.
One planet rules both an angle and a trine and is placed in an angle or trine: it becomes the chart's yoga-karaka, the planet most able to lift status and fortune.

For Aries rising, Jupiter and the Sun act as benefics; Saturn, Mercury and Venus act as malefics. Mars, although it also rules the 8th, supports whichever planets are giving good results. A Saturn-Jupiter conjunction does not by itself make a raja yoga here, and Jupiter under a malefic's sway turns unhelpful.
For Taurus rising, Saturn and the Sun are auspicious and Saturn is the raja-yoga planet; Jupiter, Venus and the Moon act as malefics; Mercury gives only mildly good results.
For Gemini rising, Venus is the one benefic; Mars, Jupiter and the Sun act as malefics. As for Aries, a Saturn-Jupiter conjunction does not by itself give a raja yoga.

For Cancer rising, Mars, Jupiter and the Moon act as benefics, and Mars is the full yoga-karaka; Venus and Mercury act as malefics. Saturn and the Sun give good results only when associated with benefics.

For Leo rising, Mars, Jupiter and the Sun act as benefics; Mercury, Venus and Saturn act as malefics. A Jupiter-Venus conjunction is not auspicious merely by being a conjunction. The Moon gives good results when associated with a benefic.

For Virgo rising, Mercury and Venus act as benefics and together are the yoga-karakas; Mars, Jupiter and the Moon act as malefics. The Sun gives results according to the planets it is associated with.
For Libra rising, Saturn and Mercury act as benefics, and the Moon and Mercury together produce raja yoga; Jupiter, the Sun and Mars act as malefics. Venus is neutral.
For Scorpio rising, Jupiter and the Moon act as benefics, and the Sun and Moon together are the yoga-karakas; Venus, Mercury and Saturn act as malefics. Mars is neutral.
For Sagittarius rising, Mars and the Sun act as benefics, and the Sun and Mercury together are the yoga-karakas; Venus is the one malefic. Jupiter is neutral.
For Capricorn rising, Venus and Mercury act as benefics and Venus is the outstanding yoga-karaka; Mars, Jupiter and the Moon act as malefics. The Sun is neutral.
For Aquarius rising, Venus and Saturn act as benefics and Venus is the sole raja-yoga planet; Jupiter, the Moon and Mars act as malefics. Mercury gives middling results.
For Pisces rising, Mars and the Moon act as benefics, and Mars with Jupiter produces a yoga; Saturn, Venus, the Sun and Mercury act as malefics.
